defects.class: off-by-one stack read / NULL dereference reproduced from the authority
defects.description: EVP_PKEY_CTX_get_keygen_info accepted idx == keygen_info_count as in range, while EVP_PKEY_generate attaches a two-element stack array and sets count = 2: idx 2 read one int past the array. Before any generation the same comparison admitted idx 0 with keygen_info == NULL, dereferencing NULL. Both are reachable from a C caller (and from an application keygen callback) as C-valid calls; the authority has the same defect.
defects.fix: The guard is idx >= count and answers 0. Valid indices 0..count are unchanged; only the out-of-range index, previously Undefined Behaviour, now returns 0.
defects.witness: evp::pmeth_gn::tests::keygen_info_refuses_the_index_it_does_not_have pins the attached two-slot array (index 2 -> 0) and the unattached context (index 0 -> 0).

defects.class: unstated length precondition -> stack-buffer overflow / silent length truncation
defects.description: hkdf_expand_label copies context_len bytes into a 512-byte HkdfLabel buffer after writing context_len as a single byte, and hkdf_expand builds T(i-1) | info | i in a 512-byte scratch block. Neither function's contract bounded context_len, label length or info_len, so a caller passing a context above 255 produced a truncated label length plus an out-of-bounds copy, and an info above the scratch capacity overflowed it. All current TLS callers pass a transcript hash or an 8-byte ticket nonce, so the paths were latent rather than reachable from the wire.
defects.fix: hkdf_expand_label refuses out_len > u16::MAX, full label > u8::MAX and context_len > u8::MAX before writing; hkdf_expand refuses a hash size above EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE and any info_len + hash_len + 1 above 512. Valid schedule inputs are unchanged.
defects.witness: ssl::tls13_enc::tests::hkdf_expand_label_refuses_a_context_that_does_not_fit_its_length_byte (256-byte context -> 0; 32-byte SHA-256 transcript -> 1 with non-zero output).

defects.class: unchecked record/inner extent and nonce precondition
defects.description: tls13_encrypt_record copied len bytes into a TLS13_HS_BUF_LEN + 1 inner buffer and wrote len + 1 + tag_len into a two-byte record-length field without checking either bound; tls13_decrypt_record and the sealer called make_nonce with iv_len without requiring 8..=16, where make_nonce indexes iv_len - 8. transcript_update computed hs_buf_len + len and write_handshake_message computed 4 + body_len in usize, both unchecked. The record layer currently fragments at 16384 and fetches a 12-byte IV, so the valid path was unaffected.
defects.fix: checked_add guards refuse inner_len > TLS13_HS_BUF_LEN + 1 and rec_len > u16::MAX; both record paths refuse iv_len outside 8..=16; transcript_update and write_handshake_message use checked_add. Valid TLS 1.3 records produce identical bytes.
defects.witness: The pre-existing oversized-TLS1.3-flight test and the full SSL suite pass; no direct record-sealer control was added because the guard is an extent refusal above the record-layer maximum.

defects.class: failure-path release (decoded receipt leaked on nine exits)
defects.description: ossl_cms_Receipt_verify returns early on a missing msgSigDigest, digest mismatch, wrong length, content-type mismatch, missing receipt request and content-identifier mismatch after ASN1_item_unpack has built the CMS_Receipt. The authority funnels every exit through its err: label, which frees rct; the transcribed returns ran none of that cleanup, so each rejected receipt leaked the decoded structure. A peer sending malformed receipts repeatedly grows the process without bound.
defects.fix: The post-unpack body is a labelled block whose refusals break to the shared cleanup (CMS_ReceiptRequest_free(rr); m_asn1_free(rct, cms_receipt_it())). Return codes and error sites are unchanged.
defects.witness: No in-module test exists; the control needs a crafted CMS receipt fixture and is recorded as BOUNDARY NOT_RUN.

defects.description: CMS_ReceiptRequest_create0_ex passed a negative idlen straight to ASN1_STRING_set0, which every later encoder converts to a huge size_t while the length field remains negative (authority UB).
defects.fix: A negative idlen is refused at the allocation's own CMS error coordinate and the fresh request is freed; id is not adopted on that path, so the caller keeps it. Non-negative lengths are unchanged.
defects.witness: Refusal path only; no fixture added.

defects.class: int -> size_t conversion of a negative length (authority UB)
defects.description: EVP_BytesToKey passed a negative datal to EVP_DigestUpdate as usize, EVP_OpenInit passed a negative ekl to EVP_PKEY_decrypt as usize, and EVP_SealInit fed a fixed 64-byte stack key to EVP_CIPHER_CTX_rand_key before checking the context key length, then used EVP_PKEY_get_size (int) as a capacity. Each is a C-valid call that the authority also mishandles; the first three are out-of-bounds reads or writes on hostile lengths.
defects.fix: Negative datal/ekl are refused (0) after the authority's NULL-data/early-success arms, so those observables are preserved. EVP_SealInit refuses a context key length outside 0..=EVP_MAX_KEY_LENGTH before the random draw, rechecks it before the key install, and refuses EVP_PKEY_get_size <= 0.

defects.class: size_t -> int truncation feeding RSA padding length arithmetic
defects.description: rsa_sign_directly's no-digest arm, rsa_verify_directly and rsa_verify_recover passed a size_t tbslen/siglen to RSA_private_encrypt/RSA_public_decrypt/RSA_verify as int. Above INT_MAX the value becomes negative, the padding routines' flen tests are bypassed and their copy length becomes a huge size_t (authority UB).
defects.fix: Each path refuses a length above c_int::MAX before the RSA call (the sign arm uses its own 821/730 coordinates; the verify/recover arms return 0). Valid provider calls are unchanged.
defects.witness: No in-module test exists and a control needs a >2 GiB input; recorded as BOUNDARY NOT_RUN.

defects.description: SSL_add_dir_cert_subjects_to_stack computed dlen + flen + 2 in usize before comparing with the 1024-byte path buffer. The authority's sum is unchecked too; the operands are strlen results and the overflow is not reachable in a real address space, but the bound check is the kind of extent arithmetic §3 requires to be total.
defects.fix: checked_add twice, with any overflow taking the existing SSL_R_PATH_TOO_LONG arm.
defects.witness: Valid directory walk is exercised only by the full suite; no dedicated fixture.

boundary_control.reason: M13-D1 and M13-D2/D6 have direct regression controls in the library suite. The cms_ess failure-path leak (D4), the rsa_sig int-truncation refusals (D7), the record extent guards (D3) and the ssl_cert path sum (D8) have no runtime negative control in this batch: D4 needs a crafted CMS receipt fixture, D7 needs >2 GiB inputs, D3 needs an over-maximum plaintext driver, and D8's overflow is unreachable in a real address space. ASan/Miri for the repaired boundaries and authority differentials for the refusal divergences are BOUNDARY gates.

residuals: src/x509/x509_vpm.rs was not re-audited; B1's boundary record stands.
EVP_BytesToKey still takes the authority's ~2^32 unsigned loop for a negative count. That is a liveness/compatibility property, not memory unsafety, and was left as authority parity.
cms_ess ossl_cms_Receipt_verify compares the message-signature digest with a Rust slice comparison, matching the authority's memcmp (public digest, not secret data); no constant-time claim is made.

add_uris_recursive continues on a NULL OSSL_STORE_load while eof/error are clear, exactly as the authority does; a store backend that answers NULL without advancing would spin. Left as authority parity, recorded rather than repaired.

src/evp/pmeth_gn.rs and src/provider/rsa_sig.rs provider callback entries still rely on the dispatch contract's pointer validity; this batch bounded the lengths they act on, not the callers' pointer provenance.
src/evp/fetch.rs's fetch half remains unreachable (allow(dead_code)) until the EVP_MD/EVP_CIPHER classes land; its audit is a contract review, not a reachable-path result.
